The result is that the same meaningful output gets compressed into fewer, sharper hours. The fear about client responsiveness is also overstated—coverage and expectations can be designed operationally, and in practice most responsiveness problems come from bad process, not from the difference between four days and five. People who insist productivity must fall are usually smuggling in an industrial-era assumption that more hours automatically means more output, which is just false for modern desk work.
